claims.claim: A meta-analysis of over 100 Kaggle competitions found little evidence of substantial overfitting from repeated holdout set reuse.
claims.quote: Our study shows, somewhat surprisingly, little evidence of substantial overfitting. These findings speak to the robustness of the holdout method across different data domains, loss functions, model classes, and human analysts.

claims.claim: LiveBench uses frequently-updated questions from recent sources like math competitions and arXiv papers with automatic scoring against objective ground-truth values.
claims.quote: LiveBench contains questions that are based on recently-released math competitions, arXiv papers, news articles, and datasets, and it contains harder, contamination-free versions of tasks from previous benchmarks.

claims.claim: LiveBench questions are added and updated on a monthly basis to maintain contamination-free evaluation.
claims.quote: Questions will be added and updated on a monthly basis, and we will release new task

claims.claim: Theoretical bounds show multiclass prediction problems are significantly more robust to overfitting from test set reuse than binary problems.
claims.quote: Our work extends developments in understanding overfitting due to adaptive data analysis to multiclass prediction problems. It also bears out the surprising fact that multiclass prediction problems are significantly more robust to overfitting when reusing a test dataset.

claims.claim: MatheMagic generates math test instances with randomly seeded altered interpretations of numbers and operators at test time with automatically verifiable answers.
claims.quote: MatheMagic, which generates math test instances with the interpretations of numbers and operators altered, yet has automatically verifiable answers. Test instances are randomly seeded and constructed at test time

claims.claim: A retrospective holdout methodology constructs statistically indistinguishable test sets for existing benchmarks and found up to 16 percentage point score inflation on TruthfulQA.
claims.quote: Applying these methods to TruthfulQA, we construct and release Retro-Misconceptions, on which we evaluate twenty LLMs and find that some have inflated scores by as much as 16 percentage points.

claims.claim: String matching decontamination is insufficient as paraphrased test data can bypass it; an LLM-based decontamination method found 8-18% HumanEval overlap in pretraining sets.
claims.quote: we show that these methods are insufficient, and simple variations of test data (e.g., paraphrasing, translation) can easily bypass these decontamination measures. [...] we identified that 8-18% of the HumanEval benchmark overlaps.

claims.claim: The authors call for the community to actively develop fresh one-time exams to evaluate models accurately.
claims.quote: Moreover, we call for the community to actively develop fresh one-time exams to evaluate models accurately.

claims.claim: EvoBrowseComp uses a three-agent framework with live-web traversal to synthesize fresh QA pairs monthly, filtering for credibility and reasoning graph formalization.
claims.quote: we design a three-agent collaborative framework: (1) a QA synthesis agent that retrieves fresh knowledge from the live web to synthesize QA pairs; (2) an information filtering agent that filters retrieved knowledge in terms of credibility and popularity to block parametric shortcuts; and (3) a high-level guidance agent that formalizes questions into reasoning graphs

claims.claim: Test-set Stress-Test (TsT) cross-validates a text-only model on test questions to measure exploitable linguistic patterns, and Iterative Bias Pruning removes high-bias questions.
claims.quote: Our Test-set Stress-Test (TsT) cross-validates a text-only Qwen2-7B on the test set's questions and answer options, yielding a benchmark-level score and a per-question bias score s(x). Iterative Bias Pruning (IBP) removes the questions with the highest s(x) and re-diagnoses

claims.claim: New test sets built by following original ImageNet/CIFAR-10 creation processes showed accuracy drops of 3-15% on CIFAR-10 and 11-14% on ImageNet, but original gains transferred to new sets.
claims.quote: We evaluate a broad range of models and find accuracy drops of 3% - 15% on CIFAR-10 and 11% - 14% on ImageNet. However, accuracy gains on the original test sets translate to larger gains on the new test sets.

claims.claim: Four new SQuAD test sets built from Wikipedia, NYT, Reddit, and Amazon showed no adaptive overfitting on original domain but 3.8-17.4 F1 drops on new domains.
claims.quote: Despite several years of heavy test set re-use, we find no evidence of adaptive overfitting. The remaining three test sets are constructed from New York Times articles, Reddit posts, and Amazon product reviews and measure robustness to natural distribution shifts.

claims.claim: A debate-driven evaluation paradigm converts QA into adversarial debates where a fine-tuned Llama 3.1 model improved 50% to 82% on test questions but performed worse in debates.
claims.quote: Empirical results validate the robustness of the method and its effectiveness against data contamination--a Llama 3.1 model fine-tuned on test questions showed dramatic accuracy improvements (50% -> 82%) but performed worse in debates.

claims.claim: A contamination detection test using exchangeable benchmark orderings found little evidence of pervasive contamination in five publicly accessible language models.
claims.quote: Using our test, we audit five popular publicly accessible language models for test set contamination and find little evidence for pervasive contamination.

claims.claim: N-Day-Bench pulls fresh vulnerability cases monthly from GitHub security advisories, uses a sandboxed shell with three agents (Curator, Finder, Judge) where the Finder never sees the patch.
claims.quote: Each month it pulls fresh cases from GitHub security advisories, checks out the repo at the last commit before the patch, and gives models a sandboxed bash shell to explore the codebase. The Finder never sees the patch.

claims.claim: AgentSeal v5 is a deterministic audit tool that tests whether SWE-bench Pro public instances are available in training corpora.
claims.quote: We built AgentSeal v5, a deterministic audit tool, to test one narrow question: Are SWE-bench Pro public instance

claims.claim: AGI Gauntlet uses obfuscated, non-web prompt vectors to bypass dataset contamination and stress-test executive reasoning with zero leakage.
claims.quote: Using obfuscated, non-web prompt vectors, it bypasses dataset contamination to stress-test true executive reasoning—pushing models past memorized training data to the precise point where their logic collapses.

claims.claim: The unbox-audit-kit provides five factorable controls (no-corpus, wrong-corpus, pair-level precision, ≥2-LLM, multi-seed) to test if a benchmark measures corpus grounding or pretraining memorization.
claims.quote: Five factorable controls (no-corpus, wrong-corpus, pair-level precision, ≥2-LLM, multi-seed) that test whether a benchmark measures corpus grounding or pretraining memorization.

open_questions: How effective are monthly refresh cycles (LiveBench, EvoBrowseComp, N-Day-Bench) at preventing contamination given the rapid pace of model training on internet-scale data?
What is the long-term robustness of dynamic benchmarks (MatheMagic, LiveBench) against models that learn the generation process itself?
How well do retrospective holdout methods (Retro-Misconceptions) generalize across different benchmark types and domains?
What are the practical trade-offs between fresh-data practices and benchmark stability for tracking progress over time?
How do debate-driven and neuro-symbolic approaches scale to larger models and more complex tasks?
What standardization exists for contamination auditing across the field (AgentSeal, unbox-audit-kit, Proving Test Set Contamination)?
